lines.speaker: Zi
lines.monologue: The trees stopped being trees about fifty meters back. They're still standing but the bark is translucent. The leaves glow with something that isn't sunlight. The ground is soft in a way that has nothing to do with rain.
lines.lens: Movement in the canopy. Not wind — the branches are moving against the wind. Something is in the trees. Something large. Thermal signature is cold where it should be warm. Reversed biology. Or not biology at all.

lines.speaker: Lex
lines.monologue: He stopped walking. His hand was on the nearest trunk. He pressed his palm against the translucent bark and his breath caught.

lines.speaker: Lex
lines.text: This tree is alive. Not sick — alive. But the life in it is wrong. Like a song played in a key the instrument wasn't built for.
lines.monologue: He knew what this was. He'd read about grove spirits in seventeen different archives. He'd never believed he'd stand in one's home.

lines.speaker: Caelan
lines.monologue: Not him. It. He could feel the spirit the way he felt thresholds — a pressure in his chest, a tightness behind his eyes. But this was different. This was pain. Old pain. The kind that has forgotten its own beginning.

lines.speaker: Zi
lines.lens: There. The canopy is moving. Branches weaving together, separating, re-forming. It's building a body from the forest itself. Not solid — a shape made of wood and light and the memory of leaves. Thirty feet tall. Moving like water through a broken pipe. No pattern. No intention. Just force and pain.

lines.speaker: Lex
lines.text: That's a grove spirit. An old one. They tend forests. They aren't — they're not aggressive. They garden. They coax. They spend centuries encouraging a single species of moss.
lines.monologue: His voice was breaking. Not with fear. With the specific grief of watching something gentle become something wounded.

lines.speaker: Caelan
lines.text: The corruption is inside it. Deep. It doesn't know what's wrong. It just knows something is wrong and it can't make it stop.
lines.monologue: He could feel it reaching. Not for them. For the trees. Trying to tend them the way it always had. But its reach was corrupted and everything it touched twisted. A gardener whose hands had become poison without its knowledge.

lines.speaker: Zi
lines.lens: Not charging. Lurching. The way a wounded animal moves toward sound — not predatory. Confused. Looking for something familiar in a body that no longer works right.

lines.speaker: Lex
lines.monologue: He said it to Zi because Zi was the one who would make the tactical decision. He said it knowing it might not be possible. He said it anyway.

lines.speaker: Zi
lines.lens: Subdue, not destroy. Target the corrupted sections — the dark veins running through its structure. If we can sever the corruption from the host form, the spirit might stabilize. If. Large if.

lines.speaker: Caelan
lines.text: I can feel where the corruption is thickest. I'll guide you.
lines.monologue: He stepped forward. Not bravely. Simply. The way you step toward something in pain because stepping away isn't something your body will let you do.

lines.speaker: Rynn
lines.text: Watch the roots. It's pulling them up.
lines.monologue: She was already moving, positioning the group. Not a commander. A logistics expert who understood that even compassion needs a supply line.
